questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Which country drinks the most coffee and why
The problem of throwaway coffee cups and solutions
How to make better coffee at home without a machine
Why plastic bags are now charged for in UK shops
questions.why: Neil and Rob discuss disposable cups and what coffee chains are doing about them.

questions.q: What does Rob do to avoid waste?
options: He has stopped drinking coffee
He only drinks coffee at home
He always carries a reusable cup
He recycles his cups in the shop
questions.why: He says, 'I always carry a reusable cup with me.'

questions.q: What is the main problem with disposable cups?
options: Many can't be recycled, so there's a lot of waste
They make the coffee taste bad after a few minutes
They are too expensive for small cafés to buy
They are too small for the drinks people want
questions.why: Rob says many can't be recycled, so there's a lot of waste.

questions.q: What are some big chains doing now?
options: Banning disposable cups completely in all their stores
Giving free reusable cups to all their regular customers
Selling only reusable cups and no paper ones at all
Adding a charge for paper cups and discounts for your own
questions.why: Neil says some charge more for a disposable cup and give discounts for reusables.

questions.q: Why is Starbucks also working on recycling outside its shops, according to Jaz Rabadia?
options: Many customers take their cups away with them
The shops are too small for bins
The government asked them to
It is cheaper than recycling in store
questions.why: She says outside their stores 'is where a lot of our cups will end up'.

questions.q: What does Jaz Rabadia say about in-store recycling?
options: It already exists in every one of their stores
It is being introduced and will be in all stores
It has been cancelled because it cost too much
It is only available in a few London stores
questions.why: She says it's being rolled out and 'will be in all of our stores'.

questions.q: Why does Mary Creagh mention the plastic bag charge?
options: To show that charges like this don't really work
To complain about how much shops charge for bags
As an example of how paying extra changes habits
To suggest that coffee shops should sell bags too
questions.why: She says a similar psychological 'nudge' measure is needed to make people bring reusable cups.

questions.q: How have coffee shops reacted to the idea of a charge, according to Mary Creagh?
options: They have welcomed it
They haven't noticed it
They have already introduced it
They have strongly fought against it
questions.why: She says the coffee shops have been 'fighting tooth and nail'.
